drivingQuestion: Is the second purchaser forbidden to slaughter before the first, or is the first purchaser's precedence merely a claim the court will uphold?
outcomeNote: Rav Yosef's reading stands, supported by the baraita and its gloss; nothing is raised against it.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לְעִנְיַן דִּינָא תְּנַן, תְּנָא: אִם קָדַם הַשֵּׁנִי – הֲרֵי זֶה זָרִיז וְנִשְׂכָּר, זָרִיז – דְּלָא עֲבַד אִיסּוּרָא, וְנִשְׂכָּר – דְּקָאָכֵיל בִּשְׂרָא.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «Rav Yosef said: We learn» in the mishna that the first purchaser is granted precedence only «with regard to the matter of» a court «judgment,» in case the two purchasers go to court each demanding to slaughter his animal first. But there is no prohibition against the second one slaughtering his animal first if no claim is brought to court. Likewise, a Sage «taught» in a baraita: «If the second» one «preceded» him and slaughtered his animal first, «he is diligent and rewarded;» he is «diligent because he did not violate a prohibition, and» he is «rewarded because he eats meat» already that day.

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: לענין דינא תנן
moves.summary: Rav Yosef confines the mishna's precedence to a matter of court judgment
moves.about: the mishna's precedence rule is a matter for the court, not a prohibition barring the second purchaser from slaughtering first

moves.cueHe: תנא: אם קדם השני – הרי זה זריז ונשכר
moves.summary: a baraita calls the one who preceded diligent and rewarded, supporting Rav Yosef
moves.about: the baraita calling the second purchaser who preceded him diligent and rewarded

moves.summary: the baraita's two terms are glossed: no prohibition broken, and meat eaten that day
moves.about: what the baraita's words diligent and rewarded each mean — that he broke no prohibition and that he eats meat that day
